note: PM check: Tyler Allgeier (this list's #1 target this morning) is now off the board — rostered by a rival since the morning check — and Arizona's RB3/4 behind him (Bam Knight, Corey Kiner) are unproven third-string names not worth chasing. Jeremiyah Love himself remains a limited-practice, officially questionable ankle case for Sunday with no clean handcuff left in the pool. targets.why: Brock Bowers (meniscus trim) is out 'a game or two,' and Mayer moves into the Raiders' starting TE role in his absence, with Ian Thomas as the only backup depth (NFL.com, Sept. 9).
targets.asset: Fill-in starting TE in a scoring format that's thin at the position, for as long as Bowers is out — a real Week 1-2 streaming option, not a name he keeps long-term.
targets.my_team_impact: You already start Juwan Johnson and hold Isaiah Likely as TE depth, so this is a bench-quality speculative add rather than a lineup lock — worth a low-cost claim only if you'd rather hold a real Week 1-2 role than Cyrus Allen's replacement-level WR snaps.
targets.worth: unpriced — year one, no bidding history in this league yet. 12 teams on 100 FAAB chase a thinner pool than the HBGBs' 10, so HBGBs prices would read low here.
targets.confidence_why: The role vacancy itself is confirmed (Bowers out, no other TE on the depth chart), but it's a two-week rental at best and your own TE room isn't needy.
targets.competition: Unlike the HBGBs (where Mayer was claimed within hours), no Pit roster shows Raiders exposure or an acute TE hole — a quieter market here.
targets.bid: unpriced — year one, no bidding history in this league yet. 12 teams on 100 FAAB chase a thinner pool than the HBGBs' 10, so HBGBs prices would read low here.
targets.drop: Cyrus Allen — an off-the-board WR depth piece with no clear role, the weakest bench spot on your roster.

targets.why: First-round rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is on IR for at least four games, and Saints coach Dennis Moore has called Vele's role 'well-defined' entering the year (DK Network, Sept. 1). Still unclaimed a day later.
targets.asset: Saints' de facto WR2 behind Chris Olave; over his last five games of 2025 he ran a route on 84% of dropbacks (2nd on the team) and saw a target on 16% of those routes.
targets.my_team_impact: A cleaner bench WR than Cyrus Allen right now, in an offense that may be forced to throw often as an underdog. Doesn't crack your starting corps over Collins/JSN/McLaurin, but it's a real role vs. a speculative one.
targets.worth: unpriced — year one, no bidding history in this league yet. 12 teams on 100 FAAB chase a thinner pool than the HBGBs' 10, so HBGBs prices would read low here.
targets.confidence_why: Multi-game route/target trend plus a direct coach quote naming the role, but it's WR2-behind-Olave value, not a bell-cow signal — and you can only make one waiver move against a full bench this week.
targets.competition: No Pit roster currently shows an acute WR hole; a low-key claim if you have a second waiver slot to use.
targets.bid: unpriced — year one, no bidding history in this league yet. 12 teams on 100 FAAB chase a thinner pool than the HBGBs' 10, so HBGBs prices would read low here.
targets.drop: Isaiah Likely — you're already carrying Juwan Johnson at TE, so Likely is the more scoopable of your two non-starting depth pieces if you need the roster spot for both Allgeier and Vele.

targets.why: Was trending as a Week 1 waiver name behind D'Andre Swift, but a foot injury has him ruled inactive for Sunday's opener at Minnesota per beat reporting (multiple outlets, Sept. 9-10) — the situation that made him relevant this week has already resolved against him.
targets.asset: None currently — third string and inactive.
targets.my_team_impact: No fit this week; revisit only if he returns to practice and Swift's own role shows real cracks.
targets.confidence_why: Direct inactive-list reporting, not a depth-chart inference.
